title: Amid a tumultuous season, Jarren Duran is starting to take off at perfect time for Red Sox
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Jarren Duran is improving amid the Red Sox's second-half surge, showing increased offensive performance after a difficult season.
Duran has notably improved his batting average to .341 over his last 12 games, contributing to Boston's recent victories.
Red Sox manager Chad Tracy sees increased confidence in Duran, who utilizes speed on basepaths for game-changing plays.

title: Suspect arrested in fatal shooting of Dorchester man
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Hensly Dominique Jeanty, 32, arrested for the mid-July murder of Breidy Martinez in Dorchester.
Jeanty faces charges including murder and multiple firearm offenses, according to Boston Police.
The shooting incident occurred near 15 York St. on July 15; investigation is ongoing.

title: Worked killed after being pinned by tractor trailer at Mass. warehouse
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A 56-year-old man died after being pinned by a tractor trailer at Chatham Village Foods in Wareham.
The incident occurred around 9:45 a.m., and the victim was pronounced dead at 9:54 a.m. on Wednesday.
An investigation by the Plymouth County District Attorney's office into the warehouse incident is ongoing.

title: Abreu homers again, Gray gets 14th victory as Red Sox beat White Sox 4-0 for 7th straight win
author: The Associated Press
bullets: The Boston Red Sox defeated the Chicago White Sox 4-0, marking their seventh consecutive victory.
Sonny Gray earned his 14th win, allowing three hits with eight strikeouts over six innings for Boston.
Wilyer Abreu hit his 20th home run, while the Red Sox recorded their 11th shutout of the season.

title: Huge basking shark spotted off South Shore beach, white sharks appear near Maine, Cape Cod
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: A large basking shark was spotted near Scituate's Humarock Beach on August 4, attracting significant attention online.
White shark sightings, including juvenile great whites, were reported near Maine's Pine Point Beach and Cape Cod's North Beach Island.
Shark expert John Chisholm attributes increased sightings to peak shark season and improved conservation and documentation efforts.

title: Man shot to death mid-morning on Blue Hill Avenue
author: Madison Lucchesi
bullets: A man was shot and killed near 564 Blue Hill Ave. in Dorchester on Wednesday morning.
Boston police found the victim with gunshot wounds; he died later in a local hospital.
Police are investigating the shooting and urge anyone with information to contact their Homicide Unit.

title: Former MLB GM says Red Sox had ‘biggest overpay’ before trade deadline
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: The Red Sox traded for Curtis Mead from the Nationals in exchange for lefty starter Connelly Early.
Former MLB GM Jim Bowden labeled the Mead-Early trade as the 'biggest overpay' in the MLB pre-deadline trades.
Mead, expected to boost Boston's lineup, is out 6-8 weeks with a fractured wrist sustained in his debut.

title: Brockton mayor suing state, says 2025 crash involving State Trooper left him disabled
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Brockton Mayor Moises Rodrigues sues Massachusetts for negligence after a 2025 crash with a State Trooper allegedly left him partially disabled.
Rodrigues claims the crash caused injuries costing over $32,000 in medical bills and resulted in lost wages of $3,554.
The lawsuit, filed in Plymouth Superior Court, seeks a jury trial and unspecified damages; Massachusetts has until Nov. 27 to respond.

title: Grant Williams explains relationship dynamic between Jayson Tatum, Jaylen Brown
author: Conor Ryan
bullets: Grant Williams addressed the relationship between Jayson Tatum and Jaylen Brown, stating they respected each other despite not being close off-court.
Tatum and Brown played together for nine years, winning an NBA championship with the Celtics in 2024.
Tatum expressed love and respect for Brown and acknowledged external attempts to create a rift during their careers.

title: Cyclospora cases climb to 147 in Mass., but officials say season remains within historical range
author: Samantha Genzer
bullets: Massachusetts reported 147 cyclospora cases from May 1 to August 1, linked to contaminated iceberg lettuce.
Cases increased from 18 between May and July to 104 in July, with diagnosis delays common.
FDA identified Taylor Farms' recalled lettuce as linked to some cyclospora cases in Massachusetts.
